newsitem.title: USA: Orange Co. panel approves refunding plans - official.
newsitem.headline: Orange Co. panel approves refunding plans - official.

text.p: A key Orange County, Calif., advisory panel on Thursday gave the county the go-ahead to begin the process of refunding nearly $200 million of taxable pension bonds, county officials said.

The proposal calls for the county to sell up to $200 million of debt to refund outstanding 1994 Series A pension obligation bonds. MBIA Insurance, a unit of MBIA Inc, has already agreed to insure the proposed debt.
The county's Public Finance Advisory Committee voted Thursday 3-to-2 to approve the plan and related bond documents, county officials said.
In October, the advisory committee split 2-to-2 on the proposed refunding. The committee was short one member when that vote was taken.
"The next step will be to go to the Board of Supervisors for approval," said Thomas Beckett, interim director of county finance and insurance.
The county Board of Supervisors is expected to consider the refunding on November 19.
As part of the deal, the county said underwriter CS First Boston would contribute up to $4 million toward the refunding.
